@knocte, thanks for asking, and sorry this took a while. This issue led to the `extensions` input, and two releases have shipped since:

### v2.1.0: model providers from pi extensions ([release](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/releases/tag/v2.1.0))

The new `extensions` input accepts npm package specs (`name@1.2.3`, `@scope/name@^1`, `github:owner/repo#ref`) or workspace paths (`./…`). Any provider an extension registers with `pi.registerProvider()` can then be picked with `provider` / `model`. Both forms of `registerProvider` work.

A minimal workflow for a custom provider shipped as a pi extension:

```yaml
- uses: cv/pi-action@v2
  with:
    github_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    extensions: |
      @acme/pi-provider@1.4.2        # or a path: ./.pi/extensions/my-provider.ts
    provider: acme                   # the name your extension registers
    model: acme-large
  env:
    ACME_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ACME_API_KEY }}
```

Some details:
- Packages are installed into `RUNNER_TEMP` with `--ignore-scripts`, never into your repo. TypeScript runs without a build step.
- `apiKey` is resolved the same way pi does it (`$ENV_VAR`, `!command`, or a literal). If you set the `api_key` input, it takes precedence.
- Only providers are used. Tools, commands and event handlers from pi extensions are skipped with a warning in the log. OAuth logins can't run on a runner, so use an API key.

Docs: [Providers from pi extensions](https://github.com/cv/pi-action#providers-from-pi-extensions)

### v2.2.0: pi-durable extensions and more ([release](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/releases/tag/v2.2.0))

- **pi-durable extensions:** packages with `pi.durable` in their `package.json` add their tools and prompt sections to every conversation. One example is [pit](https://github.com/cv/pit)'s `pit/durable` (`extensions: github:cv/pit#v0.35.0`). New inputs: `trust_project` (off by default) and `agent_dir`. Docs: [pi-durable extensions](https://github.com/cv/pi-action#pi-durable-extensions)
- **Asynchronous questions:** when an extension asks something (`ui.confirm`, `ui.select`, `ui.input`), pi-action posts the question as a comment and the run ends. You answer by ticking a check
